title: Records made, and the Navy radio shows
summary: He discusses records with Fats Pichon, an unreleased Southland session with Jeanette, Jim Robinson and George Lewis, and Friday radio shows at the Naval Air Station.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Did you ever make any records?
Well yeah I cut a few with the Fast Peace Show and I cut records with them.
You got any of the Paul Barberin? No I didn't cut those labels with Paul.
When Paul cut those labels in California I didn't go on that trip.
Did you ever make any records for Southland?

Those records I told you about made with Jeanette and Jim Robinson, George Lewis, Paul Barberin. But I don't think those records were ever released. I don't know what happened to them. I know we made them. We went up there one day and we cut about six sides or something. Four either six sides. Had a couple of them that Jeanette sang. But after it was released I don't know because I never did hear them anywhere. Of course I made a lot of records when I was in service but they wasn't for the general public. I don't know if it was Uncle Sam himself or if he was a private consign. But we used to cut them right here at the New Orleans Naval Air Station. Every Friday. Every Friday. We had a radio show we did out there. We had a radio show. We did out there. Bob Poole was master ceremony.
We had a radio show. Bob Poole was master ceremony.

And every Friday we had a radio show. And every Friday we did a show. And well for a while out there we had Robert Till. We had a radio show. We had a radio show. We had a radio show. We had a radio show. We had a radio show. We had a radio show. And every Friday we had a radio show. And every Friday we did a show. And well for a while out there we had Robert Till. He was a lieutenant then I think. Lieutenant J.G. And he he fit in a couple times for master ceremonies. When he was in service. We cut a lot of records for overseas. But didn't it. Like I said it wasn't for sale. It was a stick like a sound.
Remember any tunes you cut with Jeanette and them? Or Joe Morales?
Or the name of them? Oh I forgot the name of them.
I guess that's been a while back. Not too long ago.
About maybe three years. Something like that.
